title: The Sweet Orchard Again
premise: Beatrix Whitlock, a celebrated cellist whose hands failed her in a catastrophic final performance, has retreated to her hometown of Sweet Orchard to run a bakery on a lease that expires in spring. When a snowstorm traps her in the orchard farmhouse with Julian Marsh, the conductor who ended her career, and Theo Vance, the lawyer who once loved her and now represents the estate suing her, the three must survive the storm and each other. Old betrayals surface: Julian's sabotage of her debut, Theo's silent complicity, and the memory of a love Beatrix buried to survive. As the lease deadline and a lawsuit hearing converge, Beatrix must decide whether justice means ruin for her enemies or freedom for herself. In the end, she chooses neither vengeance nor the stage she lost, but a new life on her own terms—reopening the bakery with Theo, playing music for joy, and letting the past stay past tense at last.
about_author: Coral Montrose is the pen name of a former music journalist who spent a decade writing obituaries for orchestras before turning to romance. She lives near an apple orchard she refuses to explain, and bakes competitively under yet another name.

chapters.title: The Last Note That Broke
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A flashback frames the catastrophic final performance: her hands seizing mid-concerto, Julian cutting her off with a raised baton. Present day, she kneads bread in Sweet Orchard, counting down the bakery lease. Emotional beat: grief disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Lease, Expiring
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The landlord's letter gives her until April to buy the bakery or lose it. Theo Vance walks into her shop—older, careful, holding a summons from the estate suing her over the failed concert's insurance. Emotional beat: the past arriving in a suit and tie.

chapters.title: What the Storm Was Promised
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Forecasters predict a record blizzard. Beatrix decides to ride out the storm at the old orchard farmhouse, her grandmother's place, to think. Theo insists on driving her; his car dies at the gate. Emotional beat: reluctant proximity.

chapters.title: Snow on the Guest Room Door
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Snowed in, Theo unpacks his guilt: he was Beatrix's lover at the time of the sabotage and said nothing. He drafts the case by firelight, hating every line. Beatrix sets rules: no past, no apologies. Emotional beat: two people negotiating a truce with history.

chapters.title: A Car in the Drift
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Headlights stall in the whiteout—a third stranded guest. Beatrix digs out the car and finds Julian Marsh, half-frozen, in town to settle the estate himself. She drags him inside because she is not the kind of person who lets a man freeze, though she considers it. Emotional beat: fury and duty at war.

chapters.title: Three Plates at the Table
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian, recovering, observes the charged silence between Beatrix and Theo and realizes the lawsuit is the least of what's unresolved. He claims he came to withdraw the case. Theo doesn't believe him. Beatrix serves soup like ammunition. Emotional beat: suspicion dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: The Cello in the Attic
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Julian finds her grandmother's cello in the attic and, before thinking, plays—beautifully. Beatrix flees to the kitchen, hands shaking, and Theo follows. She admits she hasn't touched an instrument in three years. Emotional beat: the wound reopened by kindness.

chapters.title: What Theo Signed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Julian confronts Theo privately: he knows Theo saw the pressure Julian put on Beatrix's conductor and said nothing to keep his career. Theo admits it. Their argument wakes Beatrix, who hears only fragments—enough to feel betrayed twice over. Emotional beat: confession as collateral damage.

chapters.title: Bread and Evidence
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix goes cold and methodical, baking through the night while the men sleep. She rereads the insurance claim and finds an inconsistency: the estate's timeline doesn't match her medical records. She isn't the villain of this story; she may be its witness. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Conductor's Version
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian tells Beatrix the truth he's carried: the pressure came from the orchestra's board, terrified by her rising fee, and he obeyed to save his own podium. He shows her letters. Beatrix realizes her ruin was a budget line. Emotional beat: pity arriving where hate lived.

chapters.title: Thaw, Briefly
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A warm spell opens the road. Julian leaves to confront the board, promising to testify. Alone with Theo, Beatrix lets herself remember why she loved him—then slams the door on it, terrified of a third betrayal. Emotional beat: hope treated like a hazard.

chapters.title: The Board's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Julian calls: the board offers to drop the suit if Beatrix signs a gag agreement and never plays publicly again. Theo must deliver the offer he knows she'll hate. Beatrix laughs until she cries, then asks for the lease paperwork instead. Emotional beat: dignity over settlement.

chapters.title: Hands That Remember
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Alone in the farmhouse, Beatrix opens the cello case. Her hands tremble through scales, then a phrase, then the concerto's opening. It's not the same as before—slower, imperfect, alive. Emotional beat: reclaiming the body that failed her.

chapters.title: Lease Terms
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The landlord, an old family friend, reveals the estate's lawyer tried to block her purchase—Theo, before he knew it was her. Confronted, Theo admits he ran conflicts for the firm for years, burying things, including her. Emotional beat: love and betrayal sharing one face.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Saw
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo walks the frozen orchard at night and drafts his resignation instead of his brief. He decides that if he can't undo what he did, he can stop being the man who does it. He tells Beatrix he'll testify against his own firm. Emotional beat: justice chosen over self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The lawsuit hearing in the county courthouse: Julian testifies about the board's sabotage, Theo testifies about the firm's concealment, and Beatrix takes the stand with her medical records. The suit collapses. The board's chair glares; Beatrix holds his gaze. Emotional beat: justice outside the law's original script, delivered inside it.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unsweetened
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian, career likely finished, asks Beatrix for nothing except to hear her play once. She refuses—then relents, playing alone for him in the empty courthouse, not forgiveness, but acknowledgment. He leaves Sweet Orchard by the evening train. Emotional beat: closure without absolution.

chapters.title: April, Almost
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. With the suit dead, Beatrix can buy the bakery—but the money is gone to legal fees. Theo quietly transfers his firm severance into the lease, and Beatrix must decide whether to accept a gift that tastes like penance. Emotional beat: pride versus a future.

chapters.title: The Offer She Rewrites
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix counters: not a gift, a partnership—Theo can buy in with his money and his honesty, both on the table. He signs. They bake the first batch together, flour on the summons paper. Emotional beat: love rebuilt as a contract with better terms.

chapters.title: First Recital, Forty Seats
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix hosts a small concert in the bakery after closing—neighbors, the landlord, forty folding chairs. Her hands hold. She plays her grandmother's piece, then, to her own surprise, the concerto that broke her. Emotional beat: the past tense becoming past.

chapters.title: What the Storm Left
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A year later, spring. The bakery thrives; the orchard blooms; a letter arrives from Julian, conducting again in a smaller city, at peace with smaller. Theo and Beatrix plant a new apple tree over the drift line where the three of them were stranded. Emotional beat: gratitude without forgetting.

chapters.title: Sweet Orchard, Again
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Final chapter: Beatrix closes the shop on a warm evening, cello case on one arm, Theo's hand in the other. The lease is paid through the decade. She looks at the orchard and, for the first time, doesn't count what it cost her. Emotional beat: arrival—the price of survival, finally paid in full and worth it.
